title: Dynamical phase transition in generalized Dicke model with strongly interacting trapped Rydberg ions
authors: Manish Chaudhary, Rejish Nath, Weibin Li
abstract: We study dynamical phase transitions in the generalized dissipative Dicke model in an array of trapped Rydberg ions, where their density-density interactions compete with the collective spin-phonon coupling, laser driving and dissipation. This setting offers a versatile approach to study equilibrium as well as non-equilibrium many-body phenomena, as parameters, such as the Ising interaction, laser-ion and spin-phonon coupling can be tuned. Through analyzing the mean-field phase diagram, we find a variety of distinct phases and the emergence of a tricritical point that are sensitively dependent of the interaction between Rydberg ions. We then study the quantum dynamics for a finite system size and characterize parameter dependent dynamics using the spin average, entropy, and Loschmidt echo. Distinctive signatures of the dynamical phases, such as slow relaxation and metastability, arise near the phase transition. This analysis predicts rich quantum dynamics of the finite system that link to the non-equilibrium mean-field phases. Our study widens the exploration of collective and non-equilibrium phases in Dicke models, and reveals that the Rydberg ion interaction drastically affects the phase diagram and dynamics.
summary: The paper analyzes dynamical phase transitions in a model of strongly interacting Rydberg ions coupled to phonons. Using mean-field theory and advanced quantum diagnostics like the Loschmidt echo, the authors map out complex phase diagrams influenced by ion interactions. The findings demonstrate that these interactions drastically alter both the equilibrium phases and the non-equilibrium relaxation dynamics of the system.
main_problem: The study investigates dynamical phase transitions (DPTs) occurring in a generalized dissipative Dicke model.
main_result: The analysis reveals that Rydberg ion interactions significantly modify the mean-field phase diagram, leading to distinct phases and the emergence of tricritical points. Furthermore, non-equilibrium dynamics exhibit signatures like slow relaxation near these transitions.
method: The study employs a combination of Mean-Field (MF) analysis for steady states and quantum diagnostics like the Loschmidt echo and entropy growth for finite-size, non-equilibrium dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is trapped Rydberg ions arranged in a linear array, coupled to external vibrational modes (phonons). The dynamics are governed by a Master equation incorporating Rabi coupling, spin-phonon interaction, laser driving, and dissipation.
key_observables: Spin average ($\langle \sigma_j angle$), phonon averages ($X, P$), Von Neumann entropy, Loschmidt echo, and steady-state polarization ($S_z$).
important_parameters: Rydberg interaction strength ($V_{jl}$), spin-phonon coupling ($g$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), dissipation rate ($\gamma$), and detuning ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on Mean-Field approximations, including product approximations for coupled spin and bosonic operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the ion chain setup. Figure 2 presents MF phase diagrams for different Dicke model regimes (closed, dissipative, generalized). Figure 3 illustrates system dynamics following parameter quenches.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Hamiltonian and Master equation governing the system. It then analyzes steady states using Mean-Field theory to map out the phase diagram, identifying critical points. Finally, it investigates non-equilibrium quantum dynamics using diagnostics like the Loschmidt echo to characterize relaxation pathways.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines trapped ion platforms (a key AMO system) with complex open quantum dynamics and many-body physics concepts like DPTs, making it a rich area for theoretical investigation in quantum optics.
